title: Sprint 1, task 1: Put AskMate online
where: Your AskMate lives at its own web address from today. Every task you merge makes it better.
next: Go back to the portal. Register your app's address, then your checks finish.

steps.title: Connect Madhu to your portal account
steps.body:
This is a new repo, so Madhu needs to know who you are again. You do this once per repo.
1. Click the + in the terminal panel to open a second terminal. Keep Madhu running in this one.
2. In the new terminal, type the command below. It prints a link.
3. Hold Ctrl and click the link, then click Confirm in the portal.
This step finishes by itself once you confirm.

steps.title: Meet HomeShine and AskMate
steps.body:
HomeShine sells toilets, wash basins, kitchen sinks and taps. Its shop staff cannot remember every product, so customers wait, or get wrong answers.
You build AskMate: it answers HomeShine's customers from the real product list, and never makes one up.
How AskMate replies, in four steps (open answer.py to see them):
1. Understand the question.
2. Find the products in search.py.
3. Decide: answer, ask which one, or say no.
4. Word the reply in ai.py.
Code does steps 1 to 3, so every answer can be checked. Only step 4 uses AI.

steps.title: Run AskMate on your laptop
steps.body:
Type the command below in your second terminal, then open http://127.0.0.1:8001 in your browser. Type hi, then Do you have OPC 109?.
It runs, but it still calls itself the starter, and its answers are wrong. In this sprint you fix that, one task at a time.
Leave it running: it restarts by itself each time you save. Press Ctrl+C in that terminal to stop it.

steps.title: Find where every reply is made
steps.body: Open answer.py. One function takes the customer's question and gives back AskMate's whole reply.
steps.retry: Look for the function that returns answer, action and products together.

steps.title: Predict first
steps.body: HomeShine does not sell tiles. A customer asks Do you sell tiles?. What will AskMate decide?
steps.run:
from answer import reply
print(reply('Do you sell tiles?', [])['action'])
steps.explain: Nothing was found, so AskMate says no. An honest no is far better than a made-up product.

steps.title: Meet your first customers
steps.body:
Customers say hello first. Right now AskMate tells them it is a starter, and never says which shop it works for.
Do this. Click the button and read what each customer wanted.

steps.title: Give your AskMate its own name
steps.body: The problem. Customers say hello, and AskMate calls itself a starter. It never says which shop this is.
hints: Read what the customers wanted. Which shop name must your greeting say?
Change both values: "name" and "greeting". The greeting must contain HomeShine, and must not contain the word starter.
Nearly there: "greeting": "Hello! I am ____, HomeShine's helper. Ask me about toilets, wash basins, kitchen sinks and taps."

answer.why: The greeting is the first thing every customer reads, so it says who AskMate is and whose shop it is. JSON needs double quotes around every name and value, and a comma between the two pairs.

steps.well_done: Customers know who they are talking to now. Look at your browser tab: refresh it.
steps.ask: Give your AskMate its own name, and a greeting that says it works for HomeShine.
steps.gets: a customer who says hi, Hello! or Who are you?
steps.gives: your greeting, for example Hello! I am Shiny, HomeShine's helper. Ask me about toilets, wash basins, kitchen sinks and taps.
approach: Open askmate.json. It holds two values: name and greeting.
Choose a short name and put it in name.
Write a greeting that says your name and the word HomeShine. Remove the word starter.
Keep the double quotes around each value and the comma at the end of the first line. Save.
steps.where: askmate.json, its two values. Nothing else changes.

steps.title: Commit your change
steps.body: Save your work in Git with a short note. Type these in your second terminal:
steps.cmd:
git add .
git commit -m "Give AskMate its own name"

steps.title: Send it to GitHub
steps.body: Push sends your commit to GitHub. Your checks start there.

steps.title: Make a free Render account
steps.body:
Render runs web apps for free. Your AskMate will live there, at its own address.
1. Open render.com and click Get Started.
2. Sign up with your GitHub account. Render does not ask for a card for the free plan.
3. Click Continue when you see your Render dashboard.

steps.title: Put AskMate online
steps.body:
In Render, click New +, then Web Service, then Public Git Repository. Fill in:
1. Repository URL: your repo's address on GitHub, like https://github.com/jivamruta-cohort/askmate-yourlogin.
2. Branch: main. Language: Python 3.
3. Build Command: pip install -r requirements.txt
4. Start Command: uvicorn main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port $PORT
5. Instance Type: Free. Click Deploy Web Service.
Wait until it says Live (about 3 minutes). Copy the address at the top, ending in .onrender.com, and paste it below.
It deploys main, so it still says starter. After you merge this task, it shows your new name.

steps.title: Tell the portal where your app lives
steps.body:
In Render, open your service, then Settings. Find Deploy Hook and copy it. It is a secret link: never put it in your code.
In the portal, open Your live app in the left map. Paste your app's address and the deploy hook, then click Save and check.
From now on, each time you merge, the portal tells Render to put your newest code online.
